deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected pencil draft of a legal document in German, a power of attorney (Vollmacht), dated Göttingen, 15 November 1858. It sits on the verso of a sheet in the 'Luftwellen' bundle; the neighbouring pages hold an outline of the 1859/60 shock-wave paper ('Verdichtungswellen') and a letter draft about Riemann's election to the Göttingen Society.

The upper half shows several abandoned attempts at the wording. Phrasings are crossed out, among them 'bevollmächtigen wir hiedurch den Herrn Doctor ...' and '(haben wir den Herrn Doctor ... ersucht, uns in diesem Termine zu vertreten ...)'.

The lower half is the clean version, in substance as follows. The Royal District Court (Königliches Amtsgericht) of Dannenberg has set 24 November of this year as the date for the publication (opening) of the testament of a female Riemann relative who died on 24 December 1856. It has summoned the undersigned. Since circumstances prevent them from attending, they have asked Herr Doctor [name uncertain, read as 'Bertsfeld'] to represent them at this hearing, sending him the deposit and estate certificates. They hereby authorise him to do so.

The signatories are Ida Riemann and 'Dr. B. Riemann, Professor, für sich und als Vormund seiner minderjährigen ...'. The final words, 'Schwester Helene Riemann', are struck through. Below the signatures is a struck salutation, 'Hochgeehrter Herr Doctor!', replaced by 'Mein lieber Herr Doctor!'. This suggests a covering letter to the same lawyer was about to begin.

Biographically, Riemann acted as guardian of his younger, then minor sister Helene after his father's death in 1855. The family originated near Dannenberg, since his father was pastor at Quickborn. There are no formulas, derivations or computations on this page, so there is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.

results.what: Draft power of attorney by Ida and Bernhard Riemann (also acting as guardian of a minor sister) appointing a lawyer to represent them at the publication of a deceased relative's testament before the Amtsgericht Dannenberg, 24 Nov 1858.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely biographical and legal, with no mathematical content. It confirms known facts about Riemann's family responsibilities after 1855, such as his guardianship of his younger sister. It may be of minor interest for dating the surrounding 'Luftwellen' sheets to around late 1858, but it contains no scientific result.
transcription_corrections: The name of the deceased is uncertain. The word read as 'Schwester [?]' before 'Riemann' appears in the image to be two words, plausibly 'Fräulein' plus a first name (possibly 'Emilie' or 'Clara'), rather than 'Schwester'. It needs checking against Riemann family records; the death date of 24 Dec 1856 should identify her.

In the signature block, the struck final line appears to read 'Schwester Helene Riemann'. The preceding unstruck 'minderjährigen' is followed by a struck word, so the guardianship clause was left grammatically incomplete in the draft.
The lawyer's name ('Bertsfeld') is uncertain throughout. The image could also support a reading like 'Lessfeld' or 'Bettefeld'; it is not resolvable from the scan.
The first struck line probably does not begin with 'Bittschrift'. The struck opening word is illegible and may be 'Vollmacht' or a similar heading.
In the clean text the phrase is 'unter Übersendung des Depositions- und Verlassenschein[s]'; the last word may be 'Vorlassungsschein' or 'Verlassenschafts...' and is uncertain.
